items.q: In the acute liver disease setting, what prothrombin ratio threshold denotes fulminant failure and adverse prognosis?
items.exp: Under interpretations, the text states: 'Acute INR >= 1.5: Fulminant hepatic failure (FHF): Poor prognosis.' (Book p992)

items.q: What is the clinical significance of an elevated INR in the chronic liver disease setting as annotated on this page?
opts: Not significant in acute prognostic triage
Immediate indication for urgent liver transplantation
Diagnostic confirmation of underlying hepatocellular carcinoma
items.exp: The line explicitly reads: 'Chronic setting : Not significant' regarding acute emergency triage. (Book p992)

items.q: Fill up: FibroScan utilizes transient elastography as a non-invasive tool to differentiate ______ from cirrhosis.
items.exp: FibroScan is described as a 'Non-invasive method differentiating NASH & cirrhosis.' (Book p992)

items.q: What liver stiffness measurement on FibroScan (transient elastography) indicates established cirrhosis?
items.exp: FibroScan measures stiffness where '> 7.5 kPa indicates cirrhosis.' (Book p992)

items.q: Which modality is designated as the 'Best diagnostic tool' for liver elastography, though expensive?
items.exp: MR Elastography is designated as the 'Best diagnostic tool', though expensive and typically done after confirming with FibroScan. (Book p992)

items.q: Assess the two statements on elastography: I FibroScan is a non-invasive tool that measures liver stiffness to differentiate NASH from cirrhosis. II MR Elastography is cheap and performed routinely prior to basic ultrasound.
items.exp: Statement I is true. Statement II is false because MR elastography is expensive and done after confirming with FibroScan. (Book p992)

items.q: A 45-year-old woman with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease undergoes transient elastography. The monitor displays a stiffness reading of 6.3 kPa (as shown in the device illustration). What is the clinical interpretation?
opts: The stiffness is <= 7.5 kPa, ruling out cirrhosis
The stiffness exceeds 7.5 kPa, confirming established cirrhosis
The value indicates acute fulminant hepatic necrosis
The test is non-diagnostic and must be repeated by percutaneous biopsy
items.exp: Because cirrhosis is indicated by stiffness > 7.5 kPa, a reading of 6.3 kPa rules out established cirrhosis. (Book p992)
